speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether the Ministry has conducted a study on students from Special Assistance Plan (SAP) schools for their attitudes towards inclusivity and respect for people of different cultural backgrounds; (b) if so, to what extent do the results of these studies diverge from those of students from non-SAP schools; and (c) if not, whether the Ministry will consider conducting such a study.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: In the early years of our Independence, we established English as the common working language for multi-cultural Singapore, as a practical arrangement, to access global economic opportunities and create jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: On the contrary, they were established as part of a struggle to preserve the Chinese language and culture.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: But over the years, with the dedicated efforts of the schools and the support of the community, and helped by the rise of China, they have become more popular.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Education in Singapore reflects the diversity of our society.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: We make bilingualism a cornerstone of our education policy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: We offer opportunities for students to pursue MTL at a higher level – not just through SAP schools, but also through the Elective Programme in Malay Language for Secondary Schools (EMAS), Language Elective Programmes for Chinese, Malay and Tamil, and the National Elective Tamil Programme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Government schools, clan-based and religiously-affiliated schools, SAP schools and designated schools like the madrasahs all co-exist in our education landscape.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: At the same time, we ensure that our students get to learn about the languages and cultures of other communities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: National programmes, such as Values in Action and the Outward Bound School, offer our students the chance to forge bonds across communities and social groups.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Likewise, SAP schools make substantial efforts to encourage and build the students’ understanding of other cultures, through inter-school, cluster-based and community-based activities such as camps, festive celebrations and dialogues.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Almost all SAP schools teach their students conversational Malay.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: MOE will continue our efforts in this area.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: So, regardless of what school we are from – be it SAP, independent, clan or mission-based – we must do our part to forge a united Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that we teach the students at SAP schools about other cultures, other languages and that there is social mixing between the schools.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But could I ask what would be MOE's efforts to ensure that there is social mixing within the school?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, he is asking about social mixing within the school and not about across different schools.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: SAP schools remain relevant from the broader perspective of an evolving multi-cultural Singapore, amidst a changing global dynamic.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We all know Asia is the fastest growing region in the world and we all know China is our largest trading partner.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We also know that as countries around us catch up in the learning of multiple languages, bilingualism may no longer be a unique advantage that Singaporeans possess.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: That is why we certainly would want to continue to preserve and improve on the programmes that promote the learning of Mother Tongue Languages as much as possible.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I have cited what are the various types of schools in our very diverse education landscape.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: SAP schools are uniquely positioned to immerse the students in an environment that is rich in Chinese language and culture, with the aim of developing effectively bilingual, bi-cultural talents, given the context that I have explained earlier.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: But I also want to re-assure the Member, that within the schools, the students do not just learn Chinese language and English language.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: If they want to learn the Malay language, they would be given as much support to do so.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: It also allows for social mixing as they learn the Malay language within the same school.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: This is important because it opens up the ability of our SAP school students to appreciate the Malay language and culture, and then, equips them with the skills to communicate, not just with students within the same school but also with peers from other schools and the community, and also, from the region.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to assure the Member that the SAP schools will continue to encourage their students to interact with peers within the school and peers from other schools as well as from the community, and give them multiple platforms to learn about and also to interact with other cultures, so that we can forge an inclusive and united Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I think if we are honest and we just look around us, look around the world, in a country where there is a majority community, they will tend to insist that the language that the majority speaks becomes the national language and then, school instruction becomes in that language.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: You do not have to look very far – just look around us.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And therefore, we use English, that is neutral to all, a common language for everyone.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is how we reconcile as a country the fact that we all have multiple levels of identity.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Two important ones are: first, we are all Singaporeans; second, we are also a member of our ethnic community.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If you are a student in a SAP school and you feel that you do not have the opportunities, come, volunteer for the Member of Parliament!

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Just get into the community, visit the hawker centres – this is Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: You do not have to confine yourself to just revolving around your classrooms.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I would say that they can do more and they have been doing more.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Many SAP school students – Senior Parliamentary Secretary Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim has met some of them – are speaking very fluent Malay, and are able to go out to the community and interact with people.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, be mindful that in Singapore, do not take extreme positions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We all have multiple levels of identity; they are all important to us, but we have always managed that and we are a society that is, a work in progress.
